decision: ADR-020 §3 (scheduler decision 2026-10-09): Action definitions NexLoop itself needs are published at deployment through trusted configuration (0050), compiled from this versioned declaration; never constructed ad hoc and never written to definition tables directly. Human-owner Actions (authority human_owner) are granted to the owner's human principal, never to service principals. v4 (dispatcher ruling 2026-10-10, NX-050): the service ontology.object.edit Capability profile, declared through Consumer.edit:1 (executed by claim_matcher, whose grant is already in service-grants). Review-approved new types reuse the tenant's published ontology.object.create / ontology.object.edit snapshots for their <Type>.create / <Type>.edit (0101); a capability definition, not a grant. v5 (NX-026): Commitment.create / Commitment.edit, executed by commitment_keeper (the edit is constrained in SQL to the transition derived from the evidence ledger, 0111), and five human-owner commitment Actions (cancel, extend, attest, condition met, mark as communication commitment) through the NX-022 governed entry; SQL refuses services and Agents even with a grant. v6 (NX-027): CommercialRecord.create / CommercialRecord.edit, executed only by commercial_recorder. v7 (NX-027): CommercialRecord.observe, the human owner's read of commercial records, costs and key results (0134). v8 (NX-028 slices 2–3, one version on top of NX-027 v7): slice 2 (D7/D9), two human requests through the governed entry's capability registry (0150): nexloop.plan.request_reevaluation (marks one active plan due now; precheck still decides) and nexloop.service.query_request (brings an unknown effect forward for the executor's one QUERY; nothing is resent). Typed on Consumer v1, the business object they concern. Slice 3 (D3–D5): nexloop.conversation.takeover / nexloop.conversation.handback, human only, typed on Consumer v1 (0152). Slice 3 (dispatcher ruling B): nexloop.message.staff_send — a staff reply written by the author of the active takeover directly into a native WebChat conversation (no effect ledger), bound to one inbound message, under ADR-023 §2.6/§2.7 like any reply (0153). v9 (NX-027, on the NX-028 registry 0124): nexloop.commitment.bind_commercial and nexloop.cost.record, human only, registered in 0140 (handlers 0121 / 0120). v10 (NX-029 slice 2, on the registry 0124): nexloop.consumer.erase, nexloop.message.erase, nexloop.retention.hold and nexloop.retention.release_hold, human owner only, registered in 0142. v11: NX-030 alert silencing (nexloop.alert.silence), human owner only, on the NX-028 registry. v12 (NX-029 slice 3, registry): nexloop.consumer.export, human owner only (0141). v13 (AT-043, registry): nexloop.incentive.issue, human owner only (0145); D2 (owner 2026-10-11): EIOS risk level low, no approval; NexLoop classifies it medium, compensated by three constraints (catalog single-issue maximum, per-Consumer period limit, tenant incentive budget). v14 (NX-035, registry 0147): nexloop.restore.open_scope, human owner only (D8). Risk settled by the owner 2026-10-11 ("全部按推荐"): EIOS risk low with no approval, NexLoop classification high (the vendored ActionGovernor, which requires approval evidence above low, is not changed). Compensating controls: owner only; opened scope by scope; a channel with unverifiable counts cannot be opened while unpaused; the restore report (replay, effect window, verification) is a precondition; every opening leaves its scope row (principal, governed intent, time) and the governed intent record. v15 (AT-043 wiring; v14 is NX-035's nexloop.restore.open_scope, merged first): text only, the D2 decision recorded in v13 and in the purpose; no published definition changes (purpose is not part of a compiled definition). v16 (0153, NX-037 prerequisite, dispatcher 2026-10-11): nexloop.real_dispatch.set, human owner only; EIOS risk low with no approval, NexLoop classification high (it is the last of three switches before an external effect; the deployment switch and the service grant exclusions stay independent). v17 (NX-053, 0154): nexloop.contact_key.revoke, human owner only; EIOS risk low with no approval, NexLoop classification high (it lets an erased identity be contacted again; reason required, audited, journaled).

actions.purpose: Governed formal Consumer property write of an accepted Claim match (NX-020); also publishes the tenant's ontology.object.edit Capability snapshot that review-approved new types reuse for <Type>.edit (NX-044/NX-050). Object and property EDIT are still decided per object.
Create the Message object of an Agent reply after the channel accepted it (NX-047); content, sender, conversation and delivery state come from the governed outbound record, never from the caller.
Publish the next immutable version of a Context strategy (budgets, quotas, trim order). Human owner only; SQL refuses services and Agents even with a grant (NX-023).

Read one model-call Manifest (sources, versions, request digest). Humans only (owner / audit role, owner decision 2026-10-09); SQL refuses services, Agents and Run credentials even with a grant; never in service-grants (NX-023).
Create the Commitment object of an enterprise commitment Claim from a delivered outbound Message (or a human extension); SQL accepts only the properties prepared from that evidence (0111).
Apply the status transition SQL derives from the evidence ledger (in progress, fulfilled, breached, cancelled, communication basis); any other edit is refused (0111).
Cancel an open, conditional or in-progress commitment with a reason (never a breached one). Human owner only; SQL refuses services, Agents and Run credentials even with a grant (NX-026).
Governed extension: a new Commitment with the new due date supersedes the old one; the old one is kept. Human owner only; SQL refuses services, Agents and Run credentials even with a grant (NX-026).
Human attestation of fulfilment (qualifying evidence) with a reason and the time it happened. Human owner only; SQL refuses services, Agents and Run credentials even with a grant (NX-026).
Record that the condition of a conditional commitment is met (v0.1: humans only, D4). Human owner only; SQL refuses services, Agents and Run credentials even with a grant (NX-026).

Mark one commitment as a communication commitment: delivered messages bound to it afterwards are qualifying evidence (D3). Human owner only; SQL refuses services, Agents and Run credentials even with a grant (NX-026).
Create the CommercialRecord of a verified signed commercial event; SQL accepts only the state derived from the record's verified events (0130).
Apply the state SQL derives from all verified events of the record, its refunds and its customer link (corrections, late events, refunds, D6 pseudonymization); any other edit is refused (0130).

Read commercial records, costs and settlements, and key results (D09 GET /commercial-observations, /costs, /metrics); human owner only, SQL refuses services, Agents and Run credentials before any grant (0134).

Ask for one reevaluation of an active plan now (cause human); the NX-024 precheck still decides whether a bounded Run starts. Human only; SQL refuses services, Agents and Run credentials even with a grant (NX-028).

Ask the executor service to query the result of an unknown or query-pending effect now (D7); never a resend, never a new idempotency key; the human holds no reconcile Action. Human only; SQL refuses services, Agents and Run credentials even with a grant (NX-028).

A person takes over one conversation or one consumer for a bounded time (default 2 h, at most 24 h); the Agent does not reply meanwhile. Human only; SQL refuses services, Agents and Run credentials even with a grant (NX-028).

Hand a takeover back: the latest unanswered message returns to normal handling, earlier ones are recorded as settled, plans are reevaluated. Human only; SQL refuses services, Agents and Run credentials even with a grant (NX-028).

A person who took the conversation over replies to one inbound message (native WebChat only; an external channel needs the effect ledger, design A). Human only; SQL refuses services, Agents and Run credentials even with a grant (NX-028).

Bind a commitment to one commercial reference (connector, kind, external id); only verified signed events of that reference become its commercial_event evidence, and only for the commitment's own Consumer. Human only through the governed entry registry (0121 handler, 0140 row).

Enter a service or labour cost (operator_entered) or correct an earlier one by supersession; never rewritten, never added across currencies. Human only through the governed entry registry (0120 handler, 0140 row).

Erase one Consumer: no new contact and no new planning at once, unknown external results reconciled first, then the keeper purges text and derived data and leaves tombstones without content (0142). Human owner only; a Consumer's own request waits for this confirmation (D1).

Erase one Message: text gone from the stream, relay copy, Claim quotes and prompts that cited it; the Message object is deleted (commitments see source_deleted, recall drops it). Human owner only (0142).
Register a legal or contractual retention hold for one Consumer or one data class; only a person can register it, never an Agent (13:33; 0142).
Release a retention hold; held data is purged by the next pass (0142).

Silence one alert rule (optionally one selector) for at most 7 days with a reason; alerts are still evaluated and recorded, the workbench only marks them. Owner only: the role manifest grants it to owner alone and the handler checks the current workbench role. Human only through the governed entry registry (0150 handler and row).

Request an export of one Consumer for the requester; assembled only through the requester's own governed reads (unreadable fields and Messages withheld, AT-003), not stored, each download audited (0141). Human owner only.

AT-043: issue a catalog incentive to one Consumer (IncentiveOffering bound to it; single-issue and per-Consumer period limits). Accepted is not issued: the executor admits it at dispatch under owner controls, the contact restriction (an attached notification is refused) and the tenant incentive budget (NXB01 refuses), then a loopback provider issues it once (0145). D2 (owner 2026-10-11): EIOS risk level low, no approval; NexLoop classifies it medium, compensated by three constraints (catalog single-issue maximum, per-Consumer period limit, tenant incentive budget). Human owner only.

EIOS risk low with no approval, NexLoop classification high, settled by the owner 2026-10-11 (compensating controls in the manifest decision, v14). Open real dispatch for one tenant/world scope of a restored database once it is verified_readonly (NX-035 §6.5, D8); when every scope is open the restore is open and the actual RPO and RTO are recorded. A channel whose restore window could not be verified stays paused (NX-022) until resumed. Owner only: the role manifest grants it to owner alone and the handler checks the current workbench role. Human only through the governed entry registry (0147 handler and row).

Open or close real dispatch of external effects (0153) for the tenant (with its data mode; only 'real' can be open) or for one of its Actions (resource id). Real dispatch needs the deployment switch REAL_DISPATCH_ENABLED, the tenant switch and the Action switch all open; each change is a control event with a new control revision, so snapshots taken before it are superseded at dispatch. It grants nothing: the trusted service grants still exclude real outbound Actions (ADR-020 §3). Owner only (role manifest v9, handler checks the current workbench role); human only through the governed entry registry (0153 handler and row).

NX-053 (0154): revoke an erased contact key (NX-029 D5) by its digest or by the erasure request, with a required reason. A revoked key no longer refuses contact; erasing the same identity again re-activates it. The revocation is journaled for restore (NX-035) without the reason. Owner only (role manifest v10, handler checks the current workbench role); human only through the governed entry registry (0154 handler and row).

0210 (owner 2026-10-18): the owner confirms an unknown effect did not happen, on the latest not_found observation of its current attempt, at least 24 h after the first unknown result and 10 min after that observation, with a confirmation reference, a reason and the provider retention confirmed. The intent and its outbox become failed and a determination is recorded; nothing is sent. The reply's inbound message is escalated for the owner's follow-up unless the owner allows its one fallback reply.

0220 (ADR-034 first step, scheduler 2026-10-18): the owner marks a Consumer's persona real, simulated_agent or synthetic, with a reason; every change has a revision and an append-only event; real again is the undo. No row means real.

0220 (AT-050 drill, scheduler 2026-10-18): the owner erases a Consumer whose persona is simulated_agent or synthetic; SQL refuses a real persona, then runs the unchanged NX-029 erasure (consumer.erase stays for real customers).

0227 (operator persona slice 1, owner 2026-10-19): the owner publishes or retires an immutable operator persona version (identity, tone, values, expression rules, scenarios, AI disclosure wording); the agent never edits one.
0227: the owner assigns one Consumer an operator persona (or clears it back to the rules), with a reason; every change is an assignment event.
0227: the owner publishes the tenant's segment rules (immutable versions; first match wins; role or Consumer property conditions) and the default persona.
0227 (owner D7/D8 2026-10-19): the tenant's AI disclosure: mode (default none), when_asked deflect or handoff, block_human_claims (default false), content label; compliance with the tenant.
0228 (operator persona slice 2, D6/D9): the owner declines or reinstates one of a consumer's communication preferences (a Claim the consumer stated), with a reason; the owner never adds a preference.

0232 (outreach slice 2; P3, P8, O1, O5): the owner sets the tenant's outreach controls: time zone, quiet hours, frequency limits, marketing switch, consent mode (opt_out default, opt_in optional), unsubscribe notice, marketing frequency, sender label; switching marketing on confirms the consent mode and is recorded. Compliance stays with the tenant.

Outreach slice 3 (P2/P5): the owner enables or disables a purpose of the current outreach purpose list for the tenant, with a reason; only listed purposes (trusted configuration outreach-purposes.v<N>); the owner never adds one.

Outreach slice 4 (design §3.1/§3.2, P1/P3/P8): the owner asks for one proactive message to a Consumer for a listed purpose (native WebChat, body within the purpose's max_chars). Accepted is not sent: the business intent id is derived from tenant, consumer, purpose, origin and day; the executor admits it at dispatch after the contact restriction, the requester's current authority, owner controls, purpose, marketing eligibility, test persona, tenant quiet hours and frequency, consumer preferences, the three real dispatch layers (closed by default) and the model budget; an unknown result is queried, never sent again. Human owner only.

Outreach slice 6 (P5): approve or reject one proactive send waiting for approval (a purpose with requires_approval), with a reason, within its 24-hour window. The approver holds the Action in their current workbench role and is never the requester. Approved is only accepted: the executor still admits it through every dispatch gate (the contact restriction first); rejected or expired is terminal. Human only.

Outreach slice 7 (design §4.4/§4.5, P8): the owner records a consumer's marketing consent granted or withdrawn, or resumes marketing after an unsubscribe, with a reason and evidence (the consumer's own inbound message or an offline evidence reference). Append-only events; the marketing gate reads them at dispatch. Human owner only.

ADR-036 (capability gap D-G2): the owner publishes the next version of a named, read-only Object Set (one object type, constant filters and sort on open property groups, a projection); evaluated at read time, no member snapshot, never writes an object.

NX-039 V4 (D39-7/8/13/14): the owner publishes the next semantic release version from one evaluated candidate (accepted, change class patch or minor as the evaluator classified it; a breaking change is closed): aliases whose text hashes to the candidate's term hashes and semantic notes of at most 200 characters; never a definition, a property or an authorization.

NX-039 V4 (D39-8/9/10): the owner rolls the semantic release back to an earlier version as a new, higher version with that version's items (items of a Consumer being erased never return); Claims are never changed, the release records the ids and the count of Claims matched through a removed alias for human review; never automatic.

NX-039 V6 (§8.5, D39-8): the owner stops or resumes evolution for one dimension of the tenant, with a reason; evaluation opening and semantic publication refuse a stopped dimension (dimension_stopped). Writes the stop switch only. Human owner only, with publish and rollback.

Capability gap P2 (owner 2026-10-20): the owner publishes the next version of a named, read-only Object View for one object type (sections with ordered properties, an optional title property, related Link types); layout only - it never grants a READ, holds no value and never writes an object.

NX-041 S2 (D2, D10): the owner creates a simulation (sim:<uuid>) or shadow (shadow:<uuid>) world with a purpose and an expiry; the world is registered active and may then receive exactly one service credential bound to it alone. Real and test are never registered. Writes the registry only. Human owner only.

NX-041 S2 (D2, D10): the owner deletes a simulation or shadow world as a whole: a summary of counts and digests (no content) is kept 30 days, its credentials are revoked and its rows leave every table in bounded, resumable passes; real and test rows are never touched. Human owner only.

NX-041 S3 (D8): the owner fills a registered, active simulation world with generated data: synthetic (Consumers, objects and session events from parameters and distributions) or structural (object types and properties from the tenant's published Object Type definitions and scaled per-type counts of real objects; never a real value, identifier, message or contact datum). Output is marked synthetic, lives in that world only (real, test and shadow are refused), never enters Claims, and leaves with the world's whole deletion. The same seed and parameters give the same output digest; generator version, seed, parameter digest and definitions digest are recorded. Human owner only.

NX-041 D10 follow-up: the owner publishes a simulation world's Action catalog - the tenant's active real Action definitions whose effect has a stand-in (S4 control.nexloop_stand_ins) copied into one registered, active sim:/shadow: world; definitions and capabilities only, no credential, authority fact or effect configuration; repeatable. Human owner only.

NX-041 S5 (D5): the owner moves the logical clock of one simulation or shadow world forward: advance by seconds, pause, resume or set its rate, with a reason; every change is an event and an audit row. Real and test run on the wall and have no clock. Writes the world's clock only. Human owner only.
